stem.text: A cyclist has a speed of $5\,\text{m s}^{-1}$ and a small car has a speed of $12\,\text{m s}^{-1}$.
Which statement does **not** give a reasonable estimate?

A.text: The kinetic energy of the cyclist is $1 \times 10^{3}\,\text{J}$.

B.text: The kinetic energy of the car is $7 \times 10^{4}\,\text{J}$.

C.text: The momentum of the cyclist is $4 \times 10^{2}\,\text{kg m s}^{-1}$.

D.text: The momentum of the car is $2 \times 10^{5}\,\text{kg m s}^{-1}$.
